questions.explain: Shared Linux file storage across AZs is EFS (Regional). EBS is block storage tied to one AZ; Multi-Attach does not change that. One Zone classes trade availability for cost.

questions.stem: A banking group keeps shared reference data (currency codes, holiday calendars) in an S3 bucket. Every account in its AWS organization must be able to read the bucket, the group creates new accounts every few weeks, and no principal outside the organization may ever get access. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: List every member account ID in the bucket policy and update the policy through a pipeline when an account is created.
options.why: It works, but the policy must change every time an account is added, which is exactly the overhead to avoid.

options.text: Share the bucket with the organization through AWS Resource Access Manager.
options.why: RAM shares resources such as subnets and Transit Gateways; S3 buckets are not shared through RAM.

options.text: Add a bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject with a condition that aws:PrincipalOrgID equals the organization ID.
options.why: The condition admits any principal from any current or future account in the organization and nobody else.

options.text: Make the bucket readable to everyone, but require requests to come through an S3 VPC gateway endpoint in each account.
options.why: Turning off Block Public Access for a bank's bucket is risky, and an aws:SourceVpce condition would need every endpoint ID listed.

questions.explain: aws:PrincipalOrgID in a resource policy is the one-line way to say 'anyone in my organization'. It scales with account creation and is a building block of a data perimeter.

questions.stem: A financial group has three lines of business (retail, corporate and insurance), each with its own OU of accounts in AWS Organizations. The CFO wants each line's spend tracked separately and wants the line's finance lead emailed when its forecast monthly spend is likely to exceed its budget. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create CloudWatch billing alarms on the EstimatedCharges metric in each member account.
options.why: Billing alarms work on actual estimated charges per account, not forecasts per line of business.

options.text: Export the Cost and Usage Report to S3, run weekly Athena queries per line of business, and email the results to each line's finance lead.
options.why: This builds a custom reporting pipeline when native budgets already forecast and alert.

options.text: Define AWS Cost Categories that group accounts by line of business, and create an AWS Budget per category with a forecasted-spend alert.
options.why: Cost Categories map accounts to lines of business, and Budgets can alert on forecasted spend for each one.

options.text: Ask each line of business to review AWS Cost Explorer every Friday and report overspending.
options.why: Manual reviews do not alert automatically and can miss overspend between reviews.

questions.explain: Organize spend (accounts, tags, Cost Categories), then control it with AWS Budgets, which can alert on actual or forecasted spend. CloudWatch billing alarms are a coarser, actual-only tool.

questions.stem: A mobile banking app emits 20,000 clickstream events per second. Analysts want the events in S3 as Apache Parquet files within a few minutes, to query with Athena, and the team does not want to manage servers or consumer code. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Send events to Amazon Data Firehose with record format conversion to Parquet using an AWS Glue table schema, delivering to S3.
options.why: Firehose is fully managed, buffers records, converts JSON to Parquet and writes to S3 within minutes.

options.text: Send events to Kinesis Data Streams and run an Auto Scaling group of EC2 consumers that batch records and write Parquet files to S3.
options.why: It works, but the team must run and scale the consumer servers.

options.text: Have the app write each event directly to S3 as its own object.
options.why: Millions of tiny JSON objects are slow and costly to query and are not Parquet.

options.text: Send events to Amazon MSK and use a self-managed Kafka Connect cluster to write to S3.
options.why: Kafka plus a Connect cluster is far more to operate than a delivery stream.

questions.explain: Data Firehose is the managed 'land streaming data in S3, Redshift or OpenSearch' service, with buffering and Parquet/ORC conversion. Choose Kinesis Data Streams or MSK when you need custom real-time consumers or replay.

questions.stem: A travel insurance company sells policies worldwide from us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Policy writes must succeed in either Region at all times, including during a full outage of the other Region, and the business accepts that a write made in one Region appears in the other within about a second. Which database solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Aurora Global Database with write forwarding enabled in the secondary Region.
options.why: Write forwarding sends writes to the single primary Region, so writes fail while that Region is down until a failover happens.

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB global tables with replicas in both Regions.
options.why: Global tables are multi-active: each Region accepts reads and writes and replicates asynchronously to the other.

options.text: A DynamoDB table in each Region with DynamoDB Streams and Lambda functions that copy changes between them.
options.why: It imitates global tables with custom code that must handle conflicts and failures.

options.text: A DynamoDB table in us-east-1 with on-demand backups copied to eu-west-1.
options.why: Only one Region accepts writes, and restoring from backups is slow and loses recent data.

questions.explain: 'Writes in every Region, always' means a multi-active database: DynamoDB global tables. Aurora Global Database has one writer Region; it fails over, it does not write everywhere.

questions.stem: During a PCI DSS assessment, an acquiring bank discovered that a production Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance holding cardholder data was created without encryption at rest. The bank needs it encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, and it can accept a short maintenance window. Which approach should a solutions architect take?

options.text: Modify the DB instance, enable storage encryption, choose the customer managed key, and apply the change immediately.
options.why: Encryption cannot be turned on for an existing unencrypted DB instance by modifying it.

options.text: Create an encrypted read replica of the instance with the customer managed key and promote it.
options.why: RDS cannot create an encrypted read replica from an unencrypted DB instance.

options.text: Turn on EBS encryption by default in the Region with the customer managed key, then reboot the DB instance.
options.why: EBS default encryption applies to new EBS volumes you create; it does not encrypt an existing RDS instance's storage, and a reboot changes nothing.

options.text: Snapshot the instance, copy the snapshot with encryption using the customer managed key, and restore from the copy.
options.why: Copying a snapshot is the supported way to add encryption; restoring the copy gives an encrypted instance to switch the application to.

questions.explain: RDS encryption at rest is chosen at creation time. To encrypt an existing database: snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption, restore, cut over. The same pattern applies to EBS volumes.

questions.stem: A bank backs up its data center servers to a physical tape library and ships tapes to an offsite vault, with 10-year retention for regulatory reasons. The tape hardware is near end of life. The bank wants to cut cost and keep its existing backup software and tape-based workflow. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?

options.text: Replace the tape library with an on-premises disk array and replicate it to a second data center.
options.why: Buying and running two disk arrays costs more than cloud archive for long retention.

options.text: Change the backup software to write directly to Amazon EFS over Direct Connect.
options.why: It changes the backup workflow and EFS is costly for 10-year archives.

options.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway and archive virtual tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.why: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library to the existing software, and Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for long retention.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode and keep EBS snapshots for 10 years.
options.why: Volume Gateway does not present tapes, and long-term snapshots cost more than Deep Archive.

questions.explain: Keep the tape workflow but drop the hardware: Tape Gateway (virtual tape library) archiving to Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive. Storage Gateway types: S3 File, FSx File, Volume, Tape.

questions.stem: An insurer runs its policy system on an Aurora MySQL cluster with one writer and four Aurora Replicas. The analytics team's heavy reporting queries run through the reader endpoint and slow down the customer-facing reads that also use it. Which solution isolates the workloads with the LEAST effort?

options.text: Create a separate Aurora cluster for analytics and copy data into it with AWS DMS.
options.why: It isolates the workloads but adds a cluster and a replication pipeline to run.

options.text: Create an Aurora custom endpoint for two larger replicas used only by analytics, and keep the customer-facing app on another custom endpoint for the other replicas.
options.why: Custom endpoints route each workload to its own set of replicas inside the same cluster.

options.text: Point the analytics team at the cluster (writer) endpoint.
options.why: Reporting would then compete with writes on the writer instance, which is worse.

options.text: Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for replicas behind the reader endpoint.
options.why: More replicas share the load but analytics and customer reads still mix on every replica.

questions.explain: Aurora endpoints: cluster (writer), reader (all replicas balanced), instance, and custom (a chosen subset). Custom endpoints isolate workloads with different shapes within one cluster.

questions.stem: A bank exposes a payments API through Amazon API Gateway. Requests are queued and processed by AWS Lambda, which calls a mainframe in the bank's data center. The mainframe fails if it receives more than 50 concurrent calls, but traffic bursts to 2,000 requests per second at month-end. Which solution protects the mainframe while still processing every request?

options.text: Increase the Lambda function's memory so each call finishes faster.
options.why: Faster functions still scale concurrency with the queue backlog, so the mainframe still sees bursts.

options.text: Use an SQS queue as the Lambda event source and set the event source mapping's maximum concurrency to 50.
options.why: Requests wait safely in the queue while the event source never runs more than 50 concurrent invocations.

options.text: Enable API Gateway caching to reduce the number of requests that reach Lambda.
options.why: Payments are unique writes; caching responses does not apply and could be dangerous.

options.text: Set API Gateway throttling to 50 requests per second and let clients retry rejected calls.
options.why: Throttling rejects excess traffic with 429 errors, pushing the problem to clients instead of absorbing it.

questions.explain: To protect a fragile downstream, buffer with a queue and cap consumer concurrency (SQS event source maximum concurrency or reserved concurrency). Throttling at the front door sheds load; queuing preserves it.

questions.stem: An insurance company's auditors found that operators reach Linux instances in private subnets through a bastion host with port 22 open to the corporate IP range, and SSH keys are shared in a wiki. The auditors require no inbound ports, access controlled by IAM, and a full log of every session's commands. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with the SSM Agent on the instances, and send session logs to S3 and CloudWatch Logs.
options.why: Session Manager needs no inbound ports or SSH keys, is authorized by IAM, and records session activity.

options.text: Keep the bastion host, restrict port 22 to the company VPN range, rotate the shared SSH keys every 30 days, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
options.why: Inbound port 22 remains open and shared keys are still used, so it fails two of the three requirements.

options.text: Deploy AWS Client VPN and let operators SSH directly to the private IPs with per-user keys.
options.why: This adds a VPN to manage and still needs inbound SSH on every instance and key distribution.

options.text: Replace the bastion with a Network Load Balancer that forwards port 22 to the instances.
options.why: This exposes SSH more broadly and records nothing about the commands run.

questions.explain: 'No bastion, no inbound ports, IAM-controlled, logged sessions' is Session Manager. The instances need the agent, an instance profile and a path to the Systems Manager endpoints (NAT or VPC interface endpoints).

questions.stem: An insurance quoting service needs 6 EC2 instances to handle peak load. The company runs it in a Region with three Availability Zones and requires that losing any one AZ cause no reduction in capacity below what peak needs. Which Auto Scaling configuration meets this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: 6 instances spread across 3 Availability Zones.
options.why: Losing one AZ leaves 4 instances, below the 6 that peak needs.

options.text: 6 instances spread across 2 Availability Zones.
options.why: Losing one AZ leaves only 3 instances.

options.text: 12 instances spread across 2 Availability Zones.
options.why: It survives an AZ loss with 6 left, but pays for 12 instances when 9 are enough.

options.text: 9 instances spread across 3 Availability Zones.
options.why: Losing one AZ leaves 6 instances, exactly the peak need, with the fewest instances.

questions.explain: Static stability: size each AZ so the remaining AZs carry full load after one fails. With N AZs and a need of C, run C / (N - 1) per AZ. More AZs means less overprovisioning.

questions.stem: A bank connects its data center to AWS through a 10 Gbps dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection. A new regulation requires all data between the data center and AWS to be encrypted at layer 2 at line rate, and the bank does not want to manage VPN appliances or lose bandwidth to IPsec tunnels. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections over a public virtual interface on the Direct Connect connection.
options.why: This encrypts traffic, but IPsec is layer 3, each tunnel has a bandwidth limit well below 10 Gbps, and VPN endpoints must be managed.

options.text: Rely on the fact that Direct Connect is a private connection that does not traverse the internet.
options.why: Private is not encrypted; the regulation explicitly demands encryption.

options.text: Enable MACsec on the dedicated connection, using a Direct Connect location and port that support it.
options.why: MACsec provides layer 2, line-rate encryption on supported dedicated connections between the bank's router and the AWS device.

options.text: Enable TLS on every application and accept that some legacy protocols remain unencrypted.
options.why: That leaves some traffic unencrypted and is not layer 2 encryption of the link.

questions.explain: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted. Options: IPsec VPN over Direct Connect (layer 3, bandwidth-limited tunnels) or MACsec on supported dedicated connections (layer 2, line rate). Read the constraint: 'line rate' and 'layer 2' point to MACsec.

questions.stem: A global insurer's 200 branch offices upload scanned claim files of 2-5 GB each to a single S3 bucket in us-east-1. Uploads from Asia and South America are slow and often fail partway through, forcing a full restart. Which combination of actions will MOST improve upload performance and reliability? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use multipart upload so large files upload in parallel parts and only failed parts are retried.
options.why: Parts upload in parallel and independently, so a network drop costs one part, not the whole file.

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and use the accelerate endpoint.
options.why: Uploads enter the nearest edge location and travel to the bucket over the AWS backbone.

options.text: Put an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the bucket with caching enabled.
options.why: Caching helps downloads; it does nothing for large uploads from branches.

options.text: Create a bucket in every Region and replicate them all into us-east-1.
options.why: This adds many buckets and replication rules, and branch tooling must choose the right bucket.

options.text: Change the bucket's storage class to S3 Express One Zone.
options.why: Express One Zone is for low-latency access within one AZ, not for long-distance uploads.

questions.explain: Large, long-distance uploads: multipart upload for parallelism and resumability, Transfer Acceleration for the network path. CloudFront caching is a download optimization.

questions.stem: A claims department runs a document-indexing script that takes about 4 minutes each hour, on a dedicated m6i.xlarge EC2 instance that runs 24/7. The script needs 2 GB of memory and reads its input from S3. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?

options.text: Run the script as an AWS Lambda function invoked hourly by an Amazon EventBridge Scheduler schedule.
options.why: Lambda bills only for the minutes the script runs and fits well within its 15-minute limit.

options.text: Keep the instance and buy a Compute Savings Plan for it.
options.why: It discounts an instance that is idle more than 90 percent of the time.

options.text: Move the script to a smaller always-on t4g instance.
options.why: A smaller instance still runs and bills all hour for 4 minutes of work.

options.text: Run the script on an Amazon EKS cluster as a Kubernetes CronJob.
options.why: A cluster's control plane and nodes cost far more than the job itself.

questions.explain: Short, scheduled jobs belong on event-driven compute (EventBridge Scheduler plus Lambda, or Fargate tasks for longer runs). Paying for idle time is the most common compute waste.
